Date: 2026-06-05 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood), Ravi Patel (CobaltCompute), Elena Smirnova (CobaltCompute), Marcus Li (CobaltCompute), Sara Gomez (CobaltCompute)
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood and CobaltCompute to explore partner integration models for GPU capacity resale / managed infra. Key topics: partner motion (resell vs referral), technical compatibility (drivers, runtimes, triton/TensorRT), private deployment options (VPC/on-prem), benchmark plan to validate throughput and quantization profiles. Action items: share decks, run benchmarks, schedule technical deep dive, legal intro.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the partnerships team, with Diego our SE. say hi.
[00:06] Ravi Patel: hi, ravi here from CobaltCompute, thanks for setting this up. Elena and Marcus are on as well.
[00:10] Diego Alvarez: great to meet you all, Diego, tech lead on inference runtime. quick agenda — intro, what you're seeing on the partner side, compatibility checks, and then next steps and benchmarks. sound ok?
[00:21] Elena Smirnova: yep sounds perfect. quick real note: we have a few customers asking for a managed LLM endpoint with strict data residency in eu-west and ap-south, and they want predictable p99 latency under 250ms for small chat models, and higher throughput for batching workloads.
[00:36] Maya Chen: cool — that lines up with a few questions: are you primarily looking to resell capacity under your brand, or do you want a deeper integration like marketplace listing or co-sell?
[00:45] Ravi Patel: good question — our business ops favours resell right now, we want to package capacity and managed service under cobalt name. but for strategic accounts, we might do co-sell. overall initial motion is resell.
[00:56] Marcus Li: from a tech perspective, we run a custom Kubernetes cluster with a mix of A100 and upcoming B110-type cards — we use a mixture of containerized TRT/TensorRT images and some Triton endpoints. driver versions are a bit conservative, NV driver 515-ish in some racks — that's been a pain.
[01:14] Diego Alvarez: ok that helps. Redwood's runtime supports Triton and common PyTorch/ONNX flows, and we do kernel selection for quantized models. we also have recommended driver matrices but we can work around older drivers with a compatibility layer — might have slight perf delta.
[01:30] Elena Smirnova: is that the Redwood Dedicated product or — I sometimes see things called Redwood Dedicatedy on slides, heh.
[01:36] Maya Chen: yep that's Redwood Dedicated (we're used to that typo). Dedicated is reserved capacity pools that you can surface under your tenancy; for resale we'd typically set up a dedicated pool that maps to your offering so you can guarantee throughput.
[01:48] Sara Gomez: commercial question: what's the typical lead time to spin up a dedicated pool if we sign an MOU?
[01:53] Maya Chen: typical is 4–6 weeks to provision and validate, earlier if you have infra ready for on-prem or private control plane. if it's a marketplace/resell it's often 6–10 weeks because of integration and billing.
[02:03] Ravi Patel: ok that timeline helps — we have a handful of leads targetting Q3, so that fits.
[02:08] Marcus Li: for benchmarks, what do you need from us? models, sequence lengths, batch sizes?
[02:14] Diego Alvarez: yes. ideal is a small matrix: 1) chat-style small model (7–13B) with streaming and p99 targets, 2) medium instruction model 30B-ish for throughput, 3) embeddings workload. for each: sequence length distributions, typical batch sizes, tokenization details. we'll propose target p50/p90/p99 and throughput.
[02:32] Elena Smirnova: note: some customers insist on KMS integration for key management — we run HashiCorp Vault in our private cloud. can Redwood integrate?
[02:41] Diego Alvarez: yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; for Dedicated we have KMS integrations as well, but we can document the flow. we'll need a short security checklist from you.
[02:50] Maya Chen: quick interjection: on compliance — do you require SOC 2 / ISO for the resell offering?
[02:55] Ravi Patel: our sales org says we need SOC 2 for enterprise customers, and some customers ask about ISO27001.
[02:59] Maya Chen: Redwood's hosted + dedicated offerings are SOC 2 Type II; we can share the compliance pack.
[03:05] Marcus Li: on the runtime side, how do you handle prefix caching and kv cache across sessions? we worry about cost on repetitive prompts.
[03:13] Diego Alvarez: we do automatic prefix and KV caching, and there's config to share cache entries across sessions when safe. that reduces token cost significantly for repeated workloads. for co-located private deployments, caching behavior is the same but you control eviction policies.
[03:28] Elena Smirnova: curious about quantization recommendations — many of our customers want to use int8 or 4-bit. do you have profiles we can share?
[03:36] Diego Alvarez: yes we produce recommended quantization profiles per model family and per hardware. Diego: we'll include a suggested quant/precision table for A100 vs B110 vs newer cards and expected perf deltas. expect +x% latency but big cost wins.
[03:50] Ravi Patel: competitors question: how are you different from Lambda or CoreWeave if we were to resell?
[03:56] Maya Chen: short answer: our emphasis is production-first controls — unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, first-class observability (per-token cost tracing), and model lifecycle features like versioned rollouts + automatic fallbacks. also our partner program has reseller pricing and co-sell support.
[04:12] Sara Gomez: will there be a partner portal or API to sync SKUs / usage?
[04:16] Maya Chen: yes, partner portal + API for quotas, billing reconciliation, and usage export. we'll share the sandbox partner API docs.
[04:25] Diego Alvarez: technical note: driver mismatches are the common headache — we may ask for a small compat job to run a few kernels and a quantized inference pass. Marcus, would that be ok to run on a dev rack?
[04:35] Marcus Li: yeah we can allocate a dev rack. we have maintenance windows monday early mornings.
[04:39] Elena Smirnova: also, we'd like to understand network egress paths — some customers want all data to stay within VPC and not cross public internet. can private control plane cover that?
[04:49] Diego Alvarez: Redwood Private supports customer-managed control plane and VPC-only routing. for Dedicated we can configure network peering and private connectivity but it depends on the model of resell — we'll detail options in the checklist.
[04:59] Ravi Patel: commercially, do you prefer signing an MSA or an MOU first? our legal tends to do an MOU before full MSA.
[05:05] Maya Chen: we do MOUs for pilots, then MSA for production. we'll connect legal.
[05:09] Diego Alvarez: ok, for the benchmark plan I'll propose specifics: target models (7B, 13B, 30B), quantization levels (fp16, int8, 4-bit where supported), sequence lengths (32/128/512), steady-state batching and streaming. we'll run p50/p90/p99 latency and tokens/sec.
[05:26] Marcus Li: sounds good. question: do you have an SDK for runtime integration and multi-tenant routing?
[05:31] Maya Chen: yes, SDKs and per-route configs for routing policies. you can route by latency, cost, or region and have fallbacks.
[05:39] Elena Smirnova: one more: monitoring retention — enterprise wants 12 months of logs sometimes. what's retention policy?
[05:45] Maya Chen: default is 90 days, enterprise add-on for 12–36 months. for partner resell we can package observability retention as part of offering.
[05:54] Ravi Patel: nice. ok final logistics: timeline to run benchmarks and get back to you?
[05:58] Diego Alvarez: we'll share a draft benchmark plan in 48–72 hours; if you can provide rack access and driver details within a week we can run initial tests the following week.
[06:08] Sara Gomez: i'll coordinate access — we'll target driver matrix and sample data by 6/11.
[06:14] Maya Chen: awesome. wrap up recap?
[06:17] Ravi Patel: recap: resell as initial GTM, pilot benchmarks (Diego), compliance and KMS supported, partner portal and billing API, timeline ~4–6 weeks to onboard for dedicated offering, legal intro.
[06:30] Maya Chen: perfect — we'll send deck and partner program doc, benchmark plan, and schedule deep dive. thanks everyone.
[06:36] Elena Smirnova: thanks, bye.
[06:38] End of recording

Notes: transcription has a few mis-hearings (Redwood Dedicatedy) and occasional dropped punctuation — typical of auto transcript. Shared links during call: partner deck (link: https://redwood.ai/partners/deck), benchmark template (link: https://redwood.ai/partners/benchmarks.xlsx).
